clue.text: Great politician spoken of as an important person

parts.note: great means big

indicators.note: something spoken of is said out loud, so the politician's name is only heard, not written

parts.note: a Whig was a member of the old British party that preceded the Liberals

explanation.surface: A great statesman whom people talk about as someone who matters.
explanation.walkthrough: WHIG said aloud sounds like WIG; the Whigs were a historic British party.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: a bigwig is a person of high rank or influence.

clue.text: Support nearly all right at the end

parts.note: to support someone is to back them
most means nearly all of something

explanation.surface: Backing almost everything until the very finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right at the end' looks like part of the wordplay but is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the backmost item sits furthest back, at the extreme rear.

clue.text: Girl's after good mirror

indicators.note: after places the girl's letters following the letter for good

parts.note: a girl is a lass, with 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A girl comes after something good: a mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a looking glass is a mirror, often just called a glass.

clue.text: Diamonds to decorate

definitions.meaning: slang for diamonds or jewellery in general
to cover a cake with sugar frosting

explanation.surface: Using diamonds as ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: underworld slang for gems, and the verb for frosting a cake.

clue.text: Composer — mostly rich and very happy

parts.note: Sir Arthur Bliss was an English composer, Master of the Queen's Music

indicators.note: mostly means the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: rich, as in a rich flavour, means full

explanation.surface: A composer, nearly wealthy and delighted with life.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Bliss was an English composer; 'mostly' trims the final L from FULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: blissful means full of joy, extremely happy.

clue.text: Inactivity of monkey without oxygen

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the monkey wraps around the gas

parts.note: a langur is an Asian leaf monkey
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A monkey deprived of air goes limp and inactive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means 'outside', so the monkey surrounds O.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: languor is a pleasant lethargy, a lack of energy or activity.

clue.text: Office staff restricted air temperature

parts.note: restricted information is secret
an air is a tune, as is an aria

explanation.surface: Office workers keep the air conditioning settings under wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective term: a secretariat is the administrative staff of an organisation.

clue.text: The last word in enduring time and space

parts.note: something enduring is firm, steadfast
amen is the word said at the very end of a prayer

explanation.surface: A philosophical musing on the final word about eternity and the cosmos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time and space' look like a pair, but 'time' is just T and 'space' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic synonym: the firmament is the sky or heavens, the vault of space.

clue.text: Free toilets just north of East Newton

indicators.note: in a down entry, north of means placed directly above

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: Free public conveniences located just above East Newton, a village.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to loosen something is to free it or slacken it.

clue.text: Lament of man about extinct bird

indicators.note: about means the man's name goes round the bird

parts.note: Ben is a man's name, standing for any man
the moa was a giant flightless bird of New Zealand, now extinct

explanation.surface: A man mourning a bird that has died out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bemoan is to express grief or regret over something.

clue.text: Arrived carrying hotel sign with name, for colour changer

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the hotel letter sits inside

parts.note: arrived means came
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone checks into a hotel with a nametag, describing a creature that changes colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the chameleon is a lizard famous for changing its skin colour.

clue.text: Vehicle to move tanker's fuel, say

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to go is to move

explanation.surface: A vehicle for shifting the fuel that a tanker carries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tanker's fuel, say' is an example of what a ship carries, not a definition of petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tanker's load of fuel is its freight, the goods it carries.

clue.text: Make a lot of church service for Mussolini?

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic Eucharist service
pro means in favour of, for
Il Duce, 'the leader', was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: Asking whether a church service supports the Italian dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a lot of' reads as 'fuss over' but means produce in quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to mass-produce is to manufacture goods in large numbers by machine.

clue.text: Place religious education before science? Not I. Rot!

parts.note: to place is to put
RE is the school subject religious education

indicators.note: Not here means the letter I is left out of the word

parts.note: taken as the word science

explanation.surface: A rant against putting RE ahead of science in the school timetable, dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rot!' looks like an exclamation of disgust but is the definition; RE is a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: putrescence is decay, the state of rotting.

clue.text: What makes cuts — in A&E that's wrong!

indicators.note: in means the wrong mark goes inside the two letters

parts.note: A&E is the accident and emergency department; its two letters are used
a cross mark, X, denotes a wrong answer

explanation.surface: Complaining that cuts made in the emergency department are wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital emergency department; the X replaces the ampersand.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an axe is a chopping tool, also used of spending cutbacks.

clue.text: Clear — chap's back in love

indicators.note: back means the words are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: net, as in a net profit, means clear after deductions
Tim is a chap's name; with 's it gives TIMS

explanation.surface: It's clear: the fellow has fallen for someone again.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone smitten is struck with infatuation.

clue.text: Original popular painting's lost millions after a month

indicators.note: after places the trimmed painting following the month

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
Aug is short for August

indicators.note: lost means the letter is dropped from the painting

parts.note: a mural is a wall painting; 's is read as 'has'

explanation.surface: A popular original painting has lost its millions in value after a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: inaugural means first, opening, the original in a series.

clue.text: Book muckspreader with 50% reduction

indicators.note: halving the word, keeping its back half

explanation.surface: A farm machine for spreading manure, at half price.
explanation.definitionFit: A reader is a book of texts for learning to read or for study.

clue.text: He sells a mobile home by the coast, perhaps

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A seller offers a mobile home beside the sea, echoing the tongue-twister 'she sells seashells'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a shell is a mollusc's home, often found on the beach.

clue.text: Supplement cosmetics

definitions.meaning: face paint such as lipstick and foundation

explanation.surface: Adding extra beauty products.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the verb phrase for topping up a shortfall, and the noun for face paint.

clue.text: Queen perhaps supporting state founder's flag

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means placed underneath

parts.note: William Penn founded Pennsylvania
a queen is an example of an ant, the colony's egg-layer

explanation.surface: The monarch upholding the banner of a nation's founder.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pennant is a long tapering flag.

clue.text: React angrily where university abandons Old English

indicators.note: abandons means the letter is left out of the university's name

parts.note: Bristol is an English city with a well-known university

explanation.surface: Angry about a university giving up teaching Old English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old English' looks like one phrase but splits into O, removed, and E, added.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bristle is to show sudden anger, like an animal raising its hackles.

clue.text: American writer's book cool about the Queen

definitions.note: names the writer, with 's as a link meaning 'is'

indicators.note: about means the frozen word goes round the royal letters

parts.note: to cool something is to ice it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: An American author's book is cool about the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambrose Bierce wrote The Devil's Dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Ambrose Bierce was a nineteenth-century American satirist and short-story writer.

clue.text: Ruler constructed from fir and ash

indicators.note: constructed from means built out of these letters in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A wooden measuring rule made of two kinds of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruler' suggests a measuring stick made of wood, but is a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Title: a sharif is an Arab prince or governor, a ruler.

clue.text: Selfishly keep house key

parts.note: G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Keeping the house key to oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to hog something is to monopolise it greedily.

clue.text: Happy with debts recorded as controversial

parts.note: content means happy, satisfied
IOUs are written notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: Pleased about writing down what is owed, which proves divisive.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something contentious causes argument or dispute.

clue.text: Old brown wire is green

parts.note: in UK mains plugs the brown wire is the live one

explanation.surface: An electrician noticing an old brown wire has turned green.
explanation.walkthrough: In British plugs the live wire is brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Colour: olive is a dull yellowish green.

clue.text: Play again on middle of March and middle of June

parts.note: re means on, concerning

indicators.note: middle of, said of each month in turn, picks the central letters of their names

explanation.surface: A broadcast repeated in mid-spring and mid-summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rerun a programme is to broadcast it again.

clue.text: Holy recluse has to make fast shortly before mass?

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: to anchor something is to fix it fast
Mass is a religious rite

explanation.surface: A holy hermit fasting briefly before attending Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make fast' suggests going without food, but means secure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an anchorite is a religious hermit who lives in seclusion.

clue.text: Poem found in ciphers released by Civil Service?

indicators.note: released by means the service letters let go of the codes, leaving the rest

parts.note: ciphers are codes

explanation.surface: A poem discovered in secret documents that the Civil Service made public.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an ode is a lyric poem addressed to a subject.

clue.text: Unusually pitched battle beside Cornish river

indicators.note: beside places the fight next to the river

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a set-to is a fight

explanation.surface: A pitched battle fought alongside a river in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitched battle' is a set phrase, but 'Unusually pitched' is the definition; Cornwall is a county in southwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: falsetto is a male voice singing above its natural range.

clue.text: Final disclosure about farmed meat

parts.note: re means about, concerning
veal is the meat of farmed calves

explanation.surface: The truth finally comes out about factory-farmed meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern noun sense: the big reveal is the climactic disclosure of a secret.
